heading: Different methods, ablations and metrics recover essentially the same IOI circuit
definition: other circuit-finding methods, ablation types and metrics recover essentially the same circuit.
summary: Method independence is contested despite several independent groups recovering overlapping circuit components. Recovered circuits vary with discovery method, ablation, metric, random seed and traversal choices.

suggested_status.by_scale: C at <1B for GPT-2 small; C at 1–10B for Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct. ? at toy, 10–100B and >100B, with no explicitly identified coverage in versions.V4.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: Script counts before checker corrections: versions.V4.verdicts.supports.studies=14, versions.V4.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=22 and versions.V4.verdicts.challenges.studies=6. On GPT-2 small IOI, near/below-chance ACDC recovery under zero ablation challenges V4 (arXiv:2304.14997#r13, arXiv:2304.14997#r16, arXiv:2304.14997#r19); SP node recovery with zero ablation/KL is instead weak partial recovery, AUC 0.605, warranting limits_scope (arXiv:2304.14997#r18). Negative Name Movers recovered with extraneous heads at low KL thresholds warrant limits_scope; their absence at every tested logit-difference threshold challenges V4 (arXiv:2304.14997#r28, arXiv:2304.14997#r29). On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct IOI, EAP-IG-inputs sum/mean-positional supports agreement with the median reference, Jaccard 1.000 (arXiv:2510.00845#R5). Other configurations still challenge convergence; EAP-IG-activations sum/patching has partial overlap, Jaccard 0.125, rather than absent recovery (arXiv:2510.00845#R2, arXiv:2510.00845#R7). Discovered circuits also disagree across seeds and traversal choices (arXiv:2605.12671#R6, arXiv:2605.12671#R25) and broader analytic specifications on GPT-2 small (arXiv:2608.13754#r1). Size-controlled coarse layer-band agreement warrants limits_scope, with flip rate 0.2706; this condition is distinct from medium-granularity comparisons and pooled functional agreement (arXiv:2608.13754#r11). These condition-specific corrections retain the basis for C at the covered scales.
suggested_status.open_questions: A result that would change the assessment would demonstrate stable head, edge and causal-role recovery under matched prompts and circuit budgets across discovery methods, ablation operators and objectives, with behavioral validation. A narrower claim about recovery of selected role classes requires its own agreement criterion.

source.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
source.authors: Kevin Wang; Alexandre Variengien; Arthur Conmy; Buck Shlegeris; Jacob Steinhardt

original_result.result: No original result is provided for this comparison.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: With KL divergence, EAP and ACDC recovered GPT-2 small’s published indirect object identification (IOI) circuit well.
Sparse-autoencoder feature attribution recovered the original circuit’s main head groups across two prompts.
Distributed alignment search (DAS) found a residual-stream direction from subject-suppressing heads that passed further validation.
CD-T recovered most heads across manually identified IOI groups, including opposing and backup name-copying heads.
EAP-IG recovered manual IOI components and connections well; EAP recovered connections similarly well.
Information flow routes agreed with activation-replacement tests (path patching) on BLOOM-560M IOI.
SVD scored how components combine using only weights, revealing almost the full GPT-2 small IOI circuit.
Direction masks emphasized known late-layer IOI heads over other GPT-2 small heads.
HAP recovered all four original subject-suppressing (S-inhibition) heads in GPT-2 small IOI.
Rerooted attribution recovered all three claimed compositions without patching when excluding layer-0 heads.
ACC++ matched ACC and agreed with other circuit-discovery methods when compared against the reference IOI circuit.
Attribution patching agreed with activation patching and recovered known IOI connections for one prompt pair.
Distributed alignment search (DAS) found a prediction-flipping residual-stream direction acting through known name-copying heads.
Using KL divergence, swap graphs recovered known name-copying, subject-suppressing, and information-sending head roles.
ACDC recovered the IOI circuit poorly with the logit-difference metric.
Replacing parts of MLP8 activations contradicted the circuit; removing a disconnected component weakened these effects.
Automated IOI recovery varied with method, objective, and ablation, sometimes excluding heads that oppose name copying.
Automated methods recovered IOI heads incompletely and reproduced model behavior worse than equally sized manual circuits.
Edge Pruning and ACDC recovered substantial but incomplete overlap with the manual IOI circuit.
High overlap with manual IOI components did not ensure EAP or EAP-IG circuits reproduced model behavior.
Singular vector tracing tracked model directions, partly recovering the original IOI circuit and adding other heads.
With few components retained, discovery methods only partly matched the manual circuit; EAP omitted subject-suppressing heads.
Path-patching procedures and the FLAP discovery method selected different IOI heads and achieved different task performance.
Pruning circuit components excluded entire layers containing several heads from the original IOI circuit.
IOI circuit agreement depended strongly on loss, ablation, and whether overlap counted components or connections.
Sparse-autoencoder discovery matched full-model performance with a larger circuit that only partly matched canonical attention heads.
Including heads from the initial layer obscured task specificity and worsened other heads’ attribution rankings.
One EAP-IG configuration exactly matched the median reference circuit in Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.
Fixed-size circuits showed partial layer-band agreement exceeding random circuits.
Frozen EAP-IG recovered nearly all published IOI heads but required many additional heads.
IOI head rankings agreed only partly across scoring methods and a method that learned their ordering.
Causal scrubbing attributed much less IOI behavior to the original circuit than mean ablation.
Attribution patching diverged for large activations and identified non-IOI attention connections.
Swapping parts of activations implicated excluded MLP8 and even a random MLP, unlike whole-component swapping.
Logit-difference swap graphs weakly recovered or lost a head’s indirect-object role depending on kernel percentile cutoffs.
Discovery with discrete representations partly recovered IOI layers but omitted pattern-copying and backup name-copying layers.
Zeroing activations often reduced ACDC and Subnetwork Probing (SP) circuit recovery to near or below chance.
Arbitrary discovery changes produced IOI edge circuits with low overlap.
Discovery methods EAP-IG and RelP recovered substantially different IOI circuits across Gemma 2 and other models.
EAP circuit-discovery variants failed to converge on the same IOI circuit in Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct.
Analytic choices produced nearly disjoint IOI circuits and frequently changed their derived conclusions.
Using continuous residual-stream activations, decision trees selected layers that poorly matched the original circuit.

The broad specification-grid study compares discovered circuits with each other, rather than validating the canonical mechanism.

wording_issues.issue: Agreement depends on the method and setting. On GPT-2 small IOI, contextual decomposition and hybrid pruning recover familiar components, while continuous-residual decision trees produce a different circuit. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct IOI, EAP-IG-activations sum/patching has partial edge-set agreement with the median reference, Jaccard 0.125; EAP-IG-inputs sum/mean-positional has complete agreement with that reference, Jaccard 1.000. These Llama comparisons concern discovered edge sets, not recovery of the original GPT-2 circuit.

On GPT-2 small IOI, ACDC canonical edge-recovery AUC with KL scoring changes from 0.869 under corrupted-activation replacement to 0.539 under zero replacement, approximately absent recovery near chance (arXiv:2304.14997). Separately, arXiv:2605.12671 compares discovered ACDC circuits: interchange ablation gives edge intersection 174 and union 608, while zero ablation gives intersection 302 and union 6951. The latter study measures structural consistency among discovered circuits, not canonical recovery against chance; its structural-overlap results alone do not establish behavioral evaluation sensitivity.

Discovery objectives, recovery scores and behavioral evaluation measures are different objects. On GPT-2 small IOI, KL versus logit-difference objectives change ACDC recovery (arXiv:2310.10348). For swap graphs on name mover 9.9, logit-difference scoring gives weak partial recovery at the 25th-percentile Gaussian-kernel width, but absent clustering at the 5th-percentile width (lw:ZSYo97kcfwtFdpcwe). The former limits scope; the latter challenges metric-independent recovery. Fractional logit-difference decrease and interchange accuracy can also give different impressions of a DAS subspace intervention (arXiv:2311.17030).

The statement leaves unspecified whether sameness means named roles, head membership, edge membership or preserved behavior. On GPT-2 small IOI, arXiv:2403.17806 reports an EAP circuit containing at least 90% of manual-circuit nodes with 0% normalized faithfulness. arXiv:2405.12522 reports a 40-head SAE circuit with logit difference 3.62 versus 3.55 for the clean model. arXiv:2605.12671 reports mutual edge IoU 0.30% across DiscoGP random initializations. Across its GPT-2 small IOI discovery grid, arXiv:2608.13754 finds greater agreement for coarse layer-band claims than detailed circuit specifications. These results distinguish structural, behavioral and claim-granularity comparisons.

Some supporting results are qualitative weight scores, mask values or observational composition rankings. These establish correspondence to selected components or roles without demonstrating the complete causal circuit. Weight and mask results lack row IDs.

method_sensitivity.what: For GPT-2 small IOI, ACDC canonical recovery is partial with corrupted activations and a KL objective (edge AUC 0.869), versus approximately absent under zero ablation. In arXiv:2605.12671, zero versus interchange ablation gives ACDC accuracy 87.50% versus 90.75% and edge density 6.76% versus 1.09%; traversal-order intersections and unions are 302 and 6951 versus 174 and 608. Structural overlap alone does not measure behavioral faithfulness or completeness. Causal scrubbing assigns the original circuit less recovered behavior than the original mean-ablation evaluation.

For GPT-2 small IOI, arXiv:2304.14997 reports negative-name-mover recovery with additional heads at a low KL threshold, but absent recovery at every tested logit-difference threshold. Separately, arXiv:2310.10348 reports overall ACDC recovery AUC 0.588 with the IOI metric versus 0.868 with KL; it does not report objective-specific negative-name-mover recovery. For swap graphs on name mover 9.9, logit difference weakens IO-token clustering with the 25th-percentile kernel and yields absent clustering with the 5th-percentile kernel, whereas KL retains distinct clusters.

Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct IOI edge sets vary across EAP-family estimators and mean versus mean-positional replacement. EAP-IG-activations with sum aggregation and patching has partial agreement with the median reference, Jaccard 0.125. EAP-IG-inputs with sum aggregation and mean-positional replacement has complete agreement with that reference, Jaccard 1.000. These comparisons concern discovered edge sets rather than recovery of the original GPT-2 head classes. EAP-IG and relevance patching also produce low IOI component overlap in the Gemma, Llama and Qwen comparisons.

EAP at high sparsity incompletely recovers S-inhibition heads; generous EAP selection followed by pruning preserves them. For GPT-2 small IOI, ACDC with KL at τ=0.00398 recovers negative name movers together with additional heads, retaining 443/32923 edges: partial canonical recovery. With logit difference, negative-name-mover recovery is absent at every tested threshold. The comparison demonstrates threshold and objective sensitivity.

method_sensitivity.factor: Random initialization, traversal order and names
method_sensitivity.what: DiscoGP and EP circuit overlap varies across random seeds; ACDC outputs change with attention-head traversal order; EAP outputs change when only IOI names vary.

An EAP circuit with substantial manual-node overlap can have zero faithfulness. SAE discovery can match full-model behavior with a larger, incompletely matching head set. These evaluations test different meanings of circuit recovery.

method_sensitivity.factor: Intervention location, scope and subspace decomposition
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT-2 small IOI, residual-stream DAS recovers a circuit-consistent position direction, while MLP8 DAS can suggest a mechanism unsupported by full-component patching. Removing the disconnected subspace component sharply reduces the MLP8 effect. In lw:RFtkRXHebkwxygDe2, a DAS subspace in a norm-matched random MLP reduces logit difference more than the MLP8 direction, challenging faithful circuit recovery; no numerical effect size is stated. The metric comparison comes from arXiv:2311.17030: MLP8-direction patching gives 46.7% fractional logit-difference decrease and 4.2% interchange accuracy.

method_sensitivity.factor: Activation type and source-layer candidate pool
method_sensitivity.what: Attribution-patching agreement is poor for residual streams and MLP0 but good for head outputs. Observational rerooted attribution distinguishes task-specific components in the restricted source pool but fails to establish layer-0 duplicate-token specificity.
Per-head NIE and witness-integrated scoring under free, half-held and held regimes agree only partly or modestly with the learned IOI head ordering.

In the GPT-2 small specification grid, fixing the evaluation metric reduces derived-claim flip rate from 0.7316 to 0.5939 but leaves substantial disagreement. Holding size fixed and reducing the claim to dominant layer band yields flip rate 0.2706; this changes both the controlled setting and the claim being compared.
